title: Match the physical order to the questions users ask
description: Choose a query shape and an ORDER BY key. The model estimates how many primary-index granules remain after pruning; it is a teaching fixture, not a ClickHouse query planner.

queries.label: Tenant dashboard
queries.detail: Filter one tenant over a bounded time window and aggregate a few metric columns.

queries.label: Event-type trend
queries.detail: Filter one event type across tenants over a bounded time window.

queries.label: User history
queries.detail: Trace one user's events in time order for support or investigation.

orderKeys.label: (tenant_id, event_date, event_time)
orderKeys.detail: Clusters each tenant's time range together. Strong for tenant dashboards; weak when tenant_id is absent.

orderKeys.label: (event_type, event_date, event_time)
orderKeys.detail: Clusters event types before time. Useful for event trends, but tenant and user lookups read broadly.

orderKeys.label: (user_id, event_time)
orderKeys.detail: Clusters each user's history. Excellent for point investigations, expensive for broad dashboards.

notice: The estimate assumes evenly distributed rows, one monthly partitioning scheme, and a fixed granule size. Real pruning depends on part layout, value distribution, compression, projections, skip indexes, query rewrites, and the exact ClickHouse version.
